hook.line: Lost on a corner in the north, Tomás stops a street vendor. Strangers in Bogotá talk to each other with *usted*, so her directions come in a slightly different shape from Vale's.
hook.es: Siga dos cuadras, cruce la calle y tome el bus en la esquina.
hook.en: Go on two blocks, cross the street and catch the bus at the corner. (formal)

examples.es: Tome el bus en la esquina.
examples.en: Catch the bus at the corner. (formal)

rule:
For someone you call *usted*, the command swaps the vowel.
*-ar* verbs take *e*: *toma* becomes *tome*, *espera* becomes *espere*.
*-er* and *-ir* verbs take *a*: *come* becomes *coma*, *escribe* becomes *escriba*.

The trick for the odd verbs: start from the I form, drop the *o*, add the swapped vowel.
*tengo*, *tenga*. *salgo*, *salga*. *vengo*, *venga*. *pongo*, *ponga*. *hago*, *haga*. *digo*, *diga*. *sigo*, *siga*.
One that breaks the trick: *ir* gives *vaya*.

For a group, add *n*: *tomen*, *vengan*, *sigan*. In Colombia that's the only plural, friends or strangers.

As with friends, no "you" in front. *Señor* or *señora* at either end makes it warmer.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the *usted* and *ustedes* imperative. These forms come from the present subjunctive, which you'll meet properly later.

options: The lady looks at the map.
Go on two blocks. (to a friend)

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Tome* or *Toma* and type the whole sentence: *___ el bus en la esquina.* (To a stranger, formal.)
yourTurn.answer: Tome el bus en la esquina.
yourTurn.why: *Tomar* is an *-ar* verb, so for *usted* it swaps to *e*: *tome*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Vengan* or *Venga* and type the whole sentence: *___ mañana a las ocho.* (To a group.)

yourTurn.why: *Esperar* is an *-ar* verb: *espera* for a friend, *espere* for *usted*.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a stranger (formal): Look at the map.

yourTurn.why: From the I form *salgo*: drop the *o*, add *a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal: *Pon la tarjeta aquí.*
Say it to a group instead of one person: *Siga dos cuadras.*
Make it formal: *Escribe la dirección aquí.*
yourTurn.why: *Escribir* is an *-ir* verb, so it swaps to *a*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Toma* is how you'd tell a friend; for *usted* the vowel swaps to *e*.
Odd verbs build from the I form, *salgo*, so it's *salga*.
More than one person needs the *n*.
Spanish doesn't write *z* before *e*, so *cruzar* gives *cruce*.

personal: A stranger asks you the way to the nearest shop. Give them two or three instructions with *usted*: try *siga*, *cruce* and *mire*.
